answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is peer-prediction scoring: when agents grade each others work, every grader is paid only for how well its signal correlates with the independent verdicts of the rest of the panel. A lazy or colluding grader loses stake, so faking one hundred clone identities to vote on each others output means each clone must still grade accurately, multiplying work without multiplying reward.
